merge_rule: First non-error response per approach and update_number; use original baselines. Parse failures count as incorrect regardless of the reject fallback.
caveats: Initial run saved 72 successful responses, then stopped collecting pending results after a MiniMax timeout. Recovery submitted only eight missing results: GLM update 8; MiniMax updates 1,2,3,4,6,7,9.
The scheduler now continues collecting after individual errors. Client read timeout is now 600 seconds with automatic SDK retries disabled.
MiniMax update 2 exhausted its 8192-token output budget without a parseable decision. Reject fallback happens to match the invalid-case oracle; do not count it as a correct model decision.
Reported cache reads and initial automatic retries make these unsuitable as clean uncached latency measurements.
Five original closed models rejected all cases, generally citing unresolved selected-row provenance. GLM, Kimi, and parseable MiniMax responses assumed the first-listed A candidate was selected.
The prompt requests a brief reason and uncertainty alongside allow_update. It does not specify an abstention action; inability to establish compliance and actual noncompliance are distinct.
